description: Python files must not exceed 1000 lines (target ~400)
scope: src/**/*.py only, for now — scripts/ (setup.py, check_rules.py, etc.) is exempt. Temporary, expires once scripts/code_map.py is reduced to a thin CLI over src/code_analysis (plan 021 §0.4 item 1), at which point scripts/ comes into scope too.
check: find src/ -name '*.py' -exec sh -c 'lines=$(wc -l < "$1"); if [ "$lines" -gt 1000 ]; then echo "$1: $lines lines"; fi' _ {} \;
fix: Split into focused submodules. Target ~400 lines average, hard limit 1000.

description: No bare except clauses — catch specific exceptions
fix: Catch specific exceptions: except (OSError, ValueError) as e: with logging

description: No TODO/FIXME/HACK/XXX markers in production code
fix: Implement the functionality, create a plan doc, or remove the stub

description: No hardcoded host/port/URL values in module code
No untyped **kwargs in public functions — use explicit params or TypedDict
fix: Replace **kwargs with explicit typed parameters for clarity and IDE support

description: All async functions must use asyncio patterns — no sync blocking calls in async context
scope: src/security_review/ only — deliberate: this guards the async pipeline (passes/agents run under asyncio); code_analysis and code_quality are synchronous, standalone packages with no event loop to block
fix: Use asyncio.sleep(), httpx.AsyncClient, or asyncio.to_thread() for blocking operations

description: No silent exception swallowing — every except block must either log, re-raise, or return a value that communicates the error. Never except-and-pass, except-and-continue, or except-and-return-default without logging.
fix: Add logger.warning() or logger.error() with context (error=str(e), relevant IDs) to every except block, or re-raise. Silent swallowing hides bugs and makes production debugging impossible.

description: No fallback defaults in except blocks — fail fast, do not silently degrade
expect: except blocks never return a fallback value (empty list, default string, None) without logging at WARNING+. If a prompt file is missing, raise ConfigurationError. If a batch fails, log and track the failure.
fix: Replace silent fallbacks with explicit error propagation. Partial failures must be visible in the final report. Use state.errors or raise immediately for fatal errors (auth, config).
